# ProcessStartForm

Auto-generated Ruby on Rails + Sidekiq project for BPMN process `Process_StartForm` (Start with form).

## Setup

```bash
cp .env.example .env
bundle install
bundle exec rspec
```

## Running with Sidekiq (HTTP Service Tasks)

HTTP service tasks whose output is not read by downstream nodes are enqueued via Sidekiq (`perform_async`). Make sure Redis is running and start both Rails and the Sidekiq worker:

```bash
redis-server
bundle exec sidekiq -C config/sidekiq.yml
bundle exec rails server
```

## Endpoint

- `GET /health`
- `POST /workflows/process_start_form/execute`

## API docs

With the server running, open `http://localhost:3000/docs/` for Swagger UI (it loads from a CDN, so it
needs internet access). The OpenAPI description is in `public/openapi.json`.

class WorkflowsController < ApplicationController
  def health
    render json: { status: "ok", workflow: "Process_StartForm" }
  end

  def execute
    payload = params.fetch(:payload, params.except(:controller, :action)).to_unsafe_h.to_hash
    result = Workflows::ProcessStartFormWorkflow.call(payload)
    render json: result, status: :ok
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true
# Auto-generated by SHTLNG FlowSpec -> Ruby on Rails Compiler
# Process ID: Process_StartForm (Start with form)

module Workflows
  class ProcessStartFormWorkflow
    attr_reader :context, :visited_nodes, :enqueued_jobs

    MAX_STEPS = 100

    def self.call(initial_context = {})
      new(initial_context).call
    end

    def initialize(initial_context = {})
      @context = initial_context.transform_keys(&:to_sym)
      @visited_nodes = []
      @enqueued_jobs = []
      @join_arrivals = Hash.new(0)
    end

    def call
      queue = [:start_1]
      steps = 0

      while (current_node = queue.shift) && steps < MAX_STEPS
        steps += 1
        @visited_nodes << current_node.to_s
        next_nodes = dispatch_node(current_node)
        queue.concat(Array(next_nodes))
      end

      {
        completed: true,
        status: @enqueued_jobs.empty? ? "completed" : "enqueued",
        visited_nodes: @visited_nodes,
        enqueued_jobs: @enqueued_jobs,
        context: @context
      }
    end

    private

    def dispatch_node(node_id)
      case node_id
      when :start_1
        execute_start1
      when :task_1
        execute_task1
      when :task_2
        execute_task2
      when :task_3
        execute_task3
      when :task_4
        execute_task4
      when :end_1
        execute_end1
      else
        raise ArgumentError, "Unknown workflow node: #{node_id}"
      end
    end

    # [start] Start (start_1)
    def execute_start1
      [:task_1]
    end

    # [user_task] Review (task_1)
    def execute_task1
      [:task_2]
    end

    # [user_task] Approve (task_2)
    def execute_task2
      form = Forms::ApprovalFormForm.new(@context.slice())
      form.validate!
      [:task_3]
    end

    # [user_task] Sign (task_3)
    def execute_task3
      form = Forms::EmbeddedSignForm.new(@context.slice())
      form.validate!
      [:task_4]
    end

    # [user_task] Extra data (task_4)
    def execute_task4
      form = Forms::ExtraDataForm.new(@context.slice(:flag, :n))
      form.validate!
      [:end_1]
    end

    # [end] Done (end_1)
    def execute_end1
      []
    end
  end
end

# The classes in these folders live in a namespace named after the folder
# (app/workflows -> Workflows::...). Without this, Rails expects top-level constants.
%w[Workflows Forms Jobs Services].each do |namespace_name|
  directory = Rails.root.join("app", namespace_name.downcase)
  next unless directory.directory?

  namespace = Object.const_set(namespace_name, Module.new)
  Rails.autoloaders.main.push_dir(directory, namespace: namespace)
end

require "rails_helper"

RSpec.describe Workflows::ProcessStartFormWorkflow, type: :workflow do
  describe ".call" do
    let(:sample_payload) do
      { name: "sample_name", age: 100, vip: true, score: 100, note: "sample_note", flag: true, n: 100 }
    end

    it "executes the workflow from start to an end event" do
      result = described_class.call(sample_payload)
      expect(result[:completed]).to be(true)
      expect(result[:visited_nodes]).to include("start_1")
    end

    it "supports formal execution trace #1 ending at end_1" do
      # Formal Trace: start_1 -> task_1 -> task_2 -> task_3 -> task_4 -> end_1
      expect("end_1").not_to be_empty
    end
  end
